newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares still vulnerable, more falls seen.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares still vulnerable, more falls seen.

text.p: Singapore stocks were seen vulnerable to more falls on Monday after plunging to new lows on broad-based institutional selling last Friday, dealers said.
The Straits Times Industrials Index (STI) ended at 1,974.37, down 15.43 points.
It managed to break key psychological support of 1,980 points and hit a 45-month low at 1,968.66.
Dealers said the market could take a breather this week due to the four-day public holiday in Hong Kong as the colony reverts to China, but poor local fundamentals weighed on sentiment.
The market was also technically weak and could tumble again once momentum picks up.
Little support was also seen coming from Wall Street, as the market focuses on local factors, dealers said.
The Dow Jones rose 33.47 points to 7,687.72 on Friday.
